tables.name: household
tables.doc: The unit this bundle describes.

tables.name: party
tables.doc: Anyone or anything that can own, owe, pay, employ, insure or be paid. Tax file numbers and passwords never enter this table.

tables.name: membership
tables.doc: A party belonging to the household for a dated range, so a baby arrives and past views stay right.

tables.name: account
tables.doc: Anything with a balance. A balance is never stored; it is the sum of postings, checked against stated balances.

tables.name: alias
tables.doc: An outside identifier for an inside thing, for a dated range. Files resolve to entities here, never by file name.

tables.name: ownership
tables.doc: Dated fractional ownership. Shares sum to 10000 per subject, basis and day.

tables.name: link
tables.doc: A dated relationship between two things, with an optional share. A loan's security, its purpose by traced principal, what a policy covers, which account serves a property, who pays a subscription. These are separate facts and one facility can serve two properties.

tables.name: category
tables.doc: The chart of income and expense. Tax relevance lives in tax_map, by date.

tables.name: instrument
tables.doc: Anything held in units: a currency, a share, an ETF, an RSU, a coin.

tables.name: asset
tables.doc: A durable thing the household cares about, on the balance sheet or not. Life-cycle facts are terms.

tables.name: activity
tables.doc: An income-producing activity with a start, an end and an owner. A rental and an ABN are the same shape, and a year's composition reads from here.

tables.name: contract
tables.doc: A standing agreement. Everything that can change lives in term.

tables.name: term
tables.doc: The one table for values that change: rates, premiums, salaries, property use, warranty dates. Names come from terms.json. Never a column on an entity.

tables.name: period
tables.doc: A month, quarter or financial year. A new year is a row, never a new workbook.

tables.name: stream
tables.doc: What should keep arriving. Coverage is expected against held.

tables.name: scope
tables.doc: Nothing has four meanings: zero, not held, does not apply, not asked. A missing row is not asked. Signals read this; metrics report coverage.

tables.name: tax_map
tables.doc: Which return label a category or event kind lands on, for a dated range. entity_kind stops SMSF rent landing on an individual's label 21.

tables.name: source
tables.doc: An immutable file. Identity is its hash. A corrected document is a new source that supersedes the old. status is a projection, computed from the supersedes chain; the row itself never changes.

tables.name: observation
tables.doc: One claim one source made, with a locator back to the place. Records what was said, including what is wrong. status is a projection, computed at rebuild. An agent-extracted observation MUST carry a quote and a locator.

tables.name: tax_return
tables.doc: A return or assessment as it happened, materialised from a tax_assessment observation, or typed from a paper return. History, not calculation. An amendment is a new version.

tables.name: tax_line
tables.doc: One line on a lodged return or assessment. Labels repeat within a return and some lines have no label, so line_id is the identity and rolls_up_to names a line_id. role stops a sum multiplying a repeated net figure or reading a memo about a spouse as your own.

planes.about: What a person decided. Original, append only.

tables.name: decision
tables.doc: One thing a person chose, with the reason and what would reopen it. Survives every rebuild. status is a projection of the latest decision on the same target.

tables.name: rule
tables.doc: The household's accumulated taste: what a descriptor means.

tables.name: recipe
tables.doc: Data that reads one family of files. Written once, cached by fingerprint, judged by the gate.

tables.name: tailoring
tables.doc: One row per piece of household tailoring: the person's sentence, the definition, an example result and the standard version it was written against. On an update the example runs; if it fails an agent rewrites from the sentence.

planes.about: Intent. Original, versioned, never mixed with actuals.

tables.name: budget
tables.doc: Monthly intent per category, versioned, so last year is judged against last year's budget.

tables.name: goal
tables.doc: A named target. A refresh cycle can back one through asset_id.

tables.name: reservation
tables.doc: Money earmarked inside an account. A reservation is an intention, not segregation; the balance does not move. Requested and applied differ, and a release names what ended it.

tables.name: scenario
tables.doc: A named what-if. A forecast is (scenario, as_of, horizon).

tables.name: assumption
tables.doc: A dated overlay on terms and rates for one scenario.

tables.name: event
tables.doc: One economic fact, recognised once.

tables.name: witness
tables.doc: Which observation supports which event, and how.

tables.name: posting
tables.doc: One side of a balanced entry. Exactly one of account_id and category_id. amount_cents is base currency and sums to zero per event; native_cents is what the account's own statement says, and L3 runs on it.

tables.name: lot
tables.doc: A parcel: units and a date, or a whole property. Five-element cost base. An unknown cost is a value: cost_known false, cost null, and a sale reports an unknown gain.

tables.name: lot_match
tables.doc: One parcel meeting one disposal. Each row is one CGT event line.

tables.name: balance
tables.doc: A materialised view: month-end balance per account, summed from postings, with how it is confirmed.

tables.name: tax_item
tables.doc: A derived per-person, per-year, per-label amount, with its method and evidence state. A draft, never advice.

tables.name: check_result
tables.doc: One law, one scope, one result.

tables.name: review_item
tables.doc: Something that needs a person, ranked by money at stake.

tables.name: metric_value
tables.doc: A materialised view: one metric, one grain, one value, with its grade and dates.

tables.name: run
tables.doc: One rebuild: what went in, what came out, what it cost.

laws.name: Conservation
laws.claim: Every event's postings sum to zero.

laws.name: Clearing
laws.claim: Every clearing account is zero at close, or each open item has an age and a named missing witness.

laws.name: Continuity
laws.claim: For every statement, opening plus movements equals closing, and each closing is the next opening, on ledger-fidelity accounts.
laws.worst: 383 of 383 stated balances disagree; first on 2020-07-01.

laws.name: One claim
laws.claim: Every active observation of an event-bearing kind is attached to exactly one event as recogniser, or is a clearing or corroborating witness, or is excluded by a decision.

laws.name: Payslip
laws.claim: Gross less sacrifice, tax and deductions, plus allowances and reimbursements, equals net; year-to-date chains; the year's payslips sum to the income statement.

laws.name: Interest
laws.claim: Interest charged is within tolerance of daily interest at the rate valid each day, net of offset.

laws.name: Holdings
laws.claim: Open lots equal the units a broker states, per instrument and date, on ledger-fidelity holdings.

laws.name: Roll-forward
laws.claim: Net worth as posted equals net worth as stated by sources, month by month, wherever every account in scope has a stated balance or valuation. The identity change-in-net-worth = income - expenses + revaluation holds by construction under L1; this law tests it against independent evidence.
laws.worst: No month has a stated balance for every account.

laws.name: Ownership
laws.claim: Shares sum to 100% per subject, basis and day.

laws.name: Timeline
laws.claim: No overlapping valid ranges for one subject and term; required terms have no gaps.

laws.name: Tax tie
laws.claim: The derived return agrees with the lodged return and notice of assessment, label by label.

laws.name: Seal
laws.claim: A locked period's hash has not changed.

laws.name: Coverage
laws.claim: Every stream has what it should for the period.

laws.name: Super tie
laws.claim: Contributions on payslips reach the fund, allowing for its lag.

laws.name: Provenance
laws.claim: Every event cites an observation, and every observation a source with a hash.

laws.name: Cap
laws.claim: Contributions and thresholds sit within the law for that date, or raise an item.

laws.name: Bound
laws.claim: Every decision resolves to a target that exists after this rebuild. An orphan goes to review and is never dropped.

laws.name: One level
laws.claim: A dollar counts at one level: an asset owned by a wrapper (SMSF, trust, company) is not counted beside the wrapper's balance. The overlap is named and only the duplicated amount is scoped out. Look-through is a view, not a second count.
laws.worst: 1 wrappers held as one value each.

laws.name: BAS sales tie
laws.claim: Net sales on the year's activity statements tie to business income on the return: G1 less 1A when G1 includes GST, G1 when it does not. Statements with no G1 are skipped.

laws.name: Plausibility
laws.claim: A value does not jump beyond a declared multiple between two observations of the same subject.

metrics.doc: Money that arrived in cash accounts, by category, excluding own transfers. A super income stream counts here under SUPER-PENSION even though it moves no net worth, because it is what a retiree lives on.
Money that left, by category. A mortgage repayment counts at its cash amount; a card purchase counts when charged, the card repayment does not.
cash.income minus cash.spending.
cash.net over cash.income.
Spending against the budget valid that month.

Income as the household's wealth sees it: gross salary, employer super, gross rent, dividends. Recognised on the date the evidence gives, which is not strict accrual; no household books wages by the day.
Expenses as incurred: interest but not principal.
Gross receipts before any cost, from payslips and activities.
Total income on the return.
Taxable income, after deductions.
Income for surcharge purposes: taxable income plus fringe benefits, salary sacrifice and net investment losses.

The same year by activity, so a business year or a parental-leave year is not one low bar. Lodged-first: a lodged year reads tax_line leaves by section; an open year reads derived items by activity; the grade says which.
Each account's balance, summed from postings.
Cash accounts net of cards.
Assets less liabilities, excluding clearing and tax position.
The same, by reporting group.
The same, split by dated beneficial ownership, conserving cents.
Liquid cash less goals' reservations.
Interest charged, as stated.
Fall in the balance.
The rate valid on a date, as known at a date.
Computed daily, net of offset. A control, never a ledger figure.
Income less costs, as earned, per income-producing activity: a rental, and later an ABN.
Purchase price, duty, legal, capital improvements.
By type, as the fund received them.
Concessional and non-concessional use against the cap for that year.
Units in open lots.
Net capital gain, after losses and the discount.
The derived draft of each return label.
Tax, levies, offsets and credits by the law of that year. A draft, never advice.
How much of the year's expected evidence is held, and what is left.
Replacement costs falling due, from asset terms.
Contracted outgoings at the price valid that month.
Expected against held.
Contracts and rates rolled forward. Stored with its as_of so it can be scored later.
This year's tax at the current run rate.
